name: Simon Property Group

logo.source: en.wikipedia.org infobox logo (Simon Property Group Logo 2014.svg)

description: Simon Property Group owns, develops and manages malls, Premium Outlets and The Mills: at December 31, 2025 it held interests in 212 US properties (108 malls, 70 Premium Outlets, 16 Mills, 6 lifestyle centers, 12 other) plus 42 properties abroad, and it owns 22.2 percent of Europe's Klepierre. Its tenants (retailers, restaurants, entertainment operators) pay rent: a fixed minimum rent per square foot under long-term leases, plus charges tied to their sales and reimbursements for taxes, utilities and marketing. Simon also earns fees for managing, leasing and developing properties owned with joint-venture partners, and it holds stakes in retail operators (Catalyst Brands, the JCPenney and SPARC retail business, plus Rue Gilt Groupe) and in Jamestown, whose results show up as income from unconsolidated entities. On October 31, 2025 it bought the remaining 12 percent of The Taubman Realty Group it did not own, which triggered a $2.9 billion non-cash gain.

businessLines.name: Lease income (malls, Premium Outlets, The Mills and other retail properties)
businessLines.shareBasis: 5,839,160 / 6,364,505, computed from the FY2025 10-K income statement
businessLines.how: Retail tenants pay monthly rent under long-term leases: fixed minimum rent and fixed common-area charges, plus variable amounts based on the tenants' reported sales and reimbursements for real estate taxes, utilities and marketing. Revenue rises with occupancy, rent per square foot on new and renewed leases, and tenant sales.
businessLines.description: Base minimum rent, tenant reimbursements and percentage rent from consolidated properties. The company has one reportable segment (real estate); properties are reported by type only through counts and statistics, not separate revenue.

revenue.note: $5,839,160 thousand; FY2024 $5,389,760 thousand; FY2023 $5,164,335 thousand. Up $449.4M in 2025 mainly from higher fixed minimum lease consideration, occupancy and property transactions (10-K MD&A).

businessLines.revenueNote: $5,839,160 thousand; FY2024 $5,389,760 thousand; FY2023 $5,164,335 thousand. Up $449.4M in 2025 mainly from higher fixed minimum lease consideration, occupancy and property transactions (10-K MD&A).

operatingProfit.note: Consolidated NOI $4,914.7M (FY2024 $4,627.0M) from the 10-K's NOI reconciliation; NOI is a company-defined non-GAAP measure of the whole portfolio, not of this revenue line alone. Operating Income Before Other Items in the same reconciliation: $3,175.4M FY2025 vs $3,092.8M FY2024.

businessLines.name: Management fees and other revenues
businessLines.how: Joint-venture and third-party owners pay Simon a contractual percentage of property revenue for management, a percentage of hard costs for development, a per-square-foot charge for leasing, and insurance premiums charged to unconsolidated properties.
businessLines.description: Management, development, leasing and insurance-premium fees, mostly from unconsolidated joint-venture properties and third parties.

businessLines.name: Other income
businessLines.how: A mixed bag of smaller earnings: interest on cash and securities, occasional land sales, franchise and mixed-use operations, and one-off lease settlements; it moves year to year (down $59.9M in 2025 mainly on interest income).
businessLines.description: Interest income, land sales, mixed-use and franchise operations, lease settlements and other items.

businessLines.name: Income from unconsolidated entities and other platform investments (below revenue)
businessLines.how: Simon owns a share of joint-venture malls and outlets and of retail and real estate companies, and books its share of their profits (or losses) plus distributions; it moves with retail results and asset sales rather than with Simon's own lease rolls.
businessLines.description: Simon's share of results from joint-venture properties, its 22.2% Klepierre stake and other platform investments (Catalyst Brands retail operations, Rue Gilt Groupe e-commerce, Jamestown). Not part of reported revenue.
